sections.html:
Banks County fills the northeast corner of Georgia, with Homer as the county seat. The cities are Baldwin, Commerce, Gillsville and Lula, and the towns are Alto, Homer and Maysville. Several of these straddle a line with Habersham, Jackson or Hall, so a mailing address can name a town that sits partly in a neighboring county. Open the parcel record to learn which tax commissioner bills you.

Growth has been brisk lately. The 2020 census counted 18,035 residents, and the mid-2025 estimate is 21,273, up 17.6% from the adjusted 2020 base. About 95.6% of residents lived in rural areas in 2020.

sections.h2: Home values and what buyers see
sections.html:
The middle household income is $77,063 for 2020-2024, and the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $278,100.

The long view is steeper than the recent one. Banks County had 6,497 people in 1960, 14,422 in 2000 and 18,395 in 2010, then slipped to 18,035 in 2020 before the newer estimate jumped. A county that nearly tripled between 1960 and 2010 has houses of very different ages, from farmhouses to recent subdivisions, and buyers compare them closely.

The tax commissioner bills and collects for the county, the state, the school board and community improvement districts. In person, go to Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547. The county payment page shows weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

Call 706-677-6204 about a bill. For your valuation, an appeal, or word that a property was sold or a business closed after January 1, call the Board of Assessors at 706-677-6223. A postmark from the U.S. Postal Service dated by midnight of the deadline counts as on time, but a postage-meter date does not.

  • Suite 7: property taxes in person
  • Tax commissioner phone: 706-677-6204
  • Board of Assessors phone: 706-677-6223

Every owner of taxable real property gets a notice each year. It shows the fair market value set by the Board of Tax Assessors and the assessed value, which state law fixes at 40%.

The assessors look at sales in groups, sorted by neighborhood, property type and use, and they adjust a whole group when market evidence says values have drifted. Any change shows on your notice. If you disagree, you have 45 days from the notice date to appeal on grounds of taxability, value or non-uniform assessment.

Bills usually arrive in September. A parcel still under appeal at that point is billed on a temporary value, the smaller of last year's value or 85% of the original notice value this year, and the bill is still due on the printed date. When the appeal ends, the commissioner decides whether a supplemental bill or a credit follows.

sections.h2: Handling the tax during a sale
sections.html:
The tax commissioner does not prorate tax between a buyer and a seller. That is settled at closing, usually with the purchaser assuming it, and your closing paperwork shows who pays. Since the tax attaches to the property, whoever holds title should confirm it is paid.

A property that sold, or a business that closed, after January 1 still owes tax for the full year, and the Board of Assessors should be told. If a mortgage company pays your tax, the office would like you to forward them a copy of the bill.

  • A missing bill is no excuse, and copies are online or at the office
  • Partial payments are accepted until the bill is paid, by arrangement at 706-677-6204
  • Write the parcel ID on a check or money order

sections.h2: If an appeal is still open at the due date
sections.html:
Pay at least the appealed amount by the due date or a 1% penalty applies. You cannot put payment off, and the assessors cannot extend the deadline. Interest of 1% per month, capped at $150, builds on the rest, and paying the full bill by the due date avoids it.

If you plan to sell during an appeal, tell your closing agent. The final figure may change, a supplemental bill or credit may follow, and you should agree in writing who keeps any refund.

Nothing is automatic, and each exemption needs its own application. The name on the deed must match the applicant, who must own, occupy and claim the home as a legal residence on January 1. Bring proof of residency and of citizenship or legal authorization, plus current registration or receipts for vehicles owned in Banks County.

A married couple counts as one applicant and gets one exemption. Once granted it renews, and a refinance does not call for a new filing. A change of name or ownership through marriage, death or divorce means reapplying with a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. A faxed or emailed application is rejected. An original must arrive, or carry a non-metered postmark, by the April 1 deadline for a first-year claim.

Forms and instructions are on the county's Tax Assessors page, and the local amounts are there too.

sections.h2: First steps for a seller with tax due
sections.html:
Call 706-677-6204 and ask what is owed on the parcel for this year and any earlier ones. If part of the balance is under appeal, say so on the same call, since the temporary-value bill applies. Then give your closing agent the amount and the Suite 7 address, 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer.

If an exemption is on the property and you are moving, tell the tax commissioner once you no longer qualify. After a change of ownership, the new owner has to apply on their own.

Gather these before you list or close: your deed or parcel ID, the latest bill, any appeal paperwork, and the contact for your mortgage servicer if it pays your tax. A cash buyer who purchases as-is skips repair requests and lender timelines, but the tax still has to be cleared out of the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Banks County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Go to Suite 7 of the Courthouse Annex at 150 Hudson Ridge, Homer, GA 30547, open weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. Mailing a payment or using the online payment link also works.

faqs.q: Will the Banks County tax commissioner divide the bill between me and the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The office stays out of buyer and seller proration. Your closing documents decide who pays.

faqs.q: Can I submit a faxed homestead form in Banks County?
faqs.a: No. An original must be received or postmarked by the deadline, and faxed or emailed copies are not accepted.

faqs.q: May I pay a Banks County bill in pieces?
faqs.a: Yes. Partial payments are accepted until the bill is satisfied, and you should call 706-677-6204 to set it up. Interest keeps accruing on what remains.

faqs.q: What if no bill ever came?
faqs.a: You still have to pay by the due date. A copy is on the county website or available from the tax commissioner.
